title: StubBookRepository default makes a forgotten bookRepository injection read as 'no duplicate found'
description:
Code review of the demo-pdo epic, 2026-08-28.

test/features/opds/screens/opds_catalog_screen_test_harness.dart:94 - buildCatalogScreen defaults bookRepository to StubBookRepository(), whose findSimilarBook returns null unconditionally. OpdsDownloadHandler._findSimilarBook (lib/features/opds/mixins/opds_download_handler.dart:189) swallows every exception and returns null, so a future dedup test that forgets 'bookRepository:' reads as 'no duplicate found' and passes for the wrong reason.

The epic traded a loud-but-rare failure for a silent one: before, the real repository at least logged '[Dedup] Pre-check failed:'. Making the stub throw does NOT surface it, because of that catch.

Fix directions to weigh: make bookRepository required on buildCatalogScreen the way the feed-list harness made it required on pumpFeedListScreen (the 33 indifferent mounts then pass StubBookRepository() explicitly), or have the stub record its calls so a suite can assert it was never reached. The first is more consistent with the sibling harness; the second is cheaper.

dependencies.title: OPDS feed list test leaks a pending sqflite timer under the full suite
dependencies.description:
test/features/opds/screens/opds_feed_list_screen_test.dart 'shows loading indicator initially' intermittently fails the full unit run with a pending 10-second timer, while passing 17/17 in isolation.

ROOT CAUSE (proven 2026-08-27): the test mounts const OpdsFeedListScreen() with no repository injected (line 119), so initState builds a real OpdsRepository (opds_feed_list_screen.dart:36). _loadFeeds awaits seedDefaultFeeds, which opens a real file database at getDatabasesPath()/books.db (database_helper.dart:16-33) and runs db.execute (opds_repository.dart:29). sqflite's txnSynchronized arms a lock-warning watchdog of exactly Duration(seconds: 10) (sqflite_common-2.5.6 database_mixin.dart:563-585, constant.dart:174). The test deliberately never settles, so it ends while that watchdog is armed. Load-dependent, not order-dependent.

CORRECTION: the cause originally recorded on this bead - databaseFactory pollution between test files - is WRONG. This file installs the ffi factory itself in its own setUpAll (lines 74-76). That theory came from log lines belonging to a different file.

The original fix direction recorded here was also wrong and would have made things worse: making sqflite setup unconditional would give opds_catalog_screen_test.dart's 33 real-repository mounts a working database, seeding 33 new instances of this same flake.

Approved fix: remove real database access from OPDS widget tests. Inject fakes at lines 85/92/119 and drop the ffi setUpAll; give opds_catalog_screen_test.dart's mount helper a stub bookRepository by default (41 mounts, only 8 inject today); split that file, which is 2136 non-comment LOC, along its ten group boundaries.

dependencies.title: DSEmptyState action rows round their ink at interior seams, not at the group's outer corners
dependencies.description: lib/design_system/components/ds_empty_state.dart:151 — every action row hard-codes InkWell(borderRadius: AppRadii.mdAll), but the splash and pressed highlight are clipped to the row's OWN box (ink_well.dart:143-152, ink_highlight.dart:117-125). So rows round corners that sit on interior seams: row 1's bottom corners, the last row's top corners, all four on middle rows. The ink pulls inward and leaves ~10pt bare wedges of secondaryBackground at each seam. Fix: per-position radii — mdAll when there is one row, else mdTop / BorderRadius.zero / mdBottom. NOT ClipRRect: nothing paints outside the container, and clipping cannot un-round a corner the ink already rounded. Found in the Phase 14 code review; the rows landed in Phase 13.
dependencies.notes:
Plan: /Users/demo/projects/project_plans/demo/todo/demo_fix_empty_state_row_radii.md
Investigation: /Users/demo/projects/project_plans/demo/investigations/demo_invest_empty_state_row_radii.md
Root cause confirmed and fix approved. Use the execution skill to implement.
NOTE: the original title/description asserted the splash overflows the container's rounded corners. Disproven — the row RRect is a strict subset of the container RRect. The real defect is the opposite: every row hard-codes AppRadii.mdAll, so interior seam corners round inward and leave bare wedges. ClipRRect would NOT fix it; per-position radii (mdAll / mdTop / zero / mdBottom) will.

title: Chapter-button enablement and the skip mixin flatten different TOC lists
description:
ROOT CAUSE (proven 2026-08-27): neither decideSkipToNext nor decideSkipToPrevious checks that the entry it selects can produce a locator - both return NavigationDecision.navigate(toc[newIndex], newIndex) unconditionally (navigation_helper.dart:120-122, 233-235). The mixin discovers the null only after deciding and silently returns (toc_skip_navigation_mixin.dart:145-148). demo's filter compensates downstream of that, in the one place that cannot fix it, and in doing so indexes a different list than the mixin.

Worked example: toc [A, B(unresolvable), C, D], reader in C. Enablement indexes filtered [A,C,D] and puts C at 1, so previous targets A and the button is enabled. The mixin indexes [A,B,C,D], puts C at 2, targets B, gets a null locator and returns. Button enabled, tap does nothing.

CORRECTION: the reasoning originally recorded here - that the filter is there on purpose because without it a button can be enabled whose tap dies - is WRONG. decideSkipToPrevious returns canNavigate: true for the unresolvable entry either way, so the button is enabled and the tap dies with or without the filter. The filter changes only index arithmetic, which is what breaks parity. It does earn its place at the tail: with toc [A, B(unresolvable)] and the reader in A, the filtered list makes decideSkipToNext take its already-at-last-chapter branch and correctly disable next.

Approved fix: add navigableToc(publication) to plugin's toc_matcher (flatten + drop entries with no locator); use it in the skip mixin, in demo's computeBoundaryState, and - per the user's Gate 2 choice - in ReaderTipProgress too, which changes its constructor from a List<Link> callback to a Publication callback and needs a cached list to keep the per-locator-event cost down. Ships as plugin 0.19.0.

Latent defect found by inspection during demo-i2q. No real book is known to trigger it.

dependencies.title: Chapter-button enablement never matches by toc= fragment
dependencies.description:
lib/features/reader/controllers/readium_navigation_controller.dart:33 reads

  curIndex = toc.indexWhere((link) => link.hrefPart.endsWith('#$tocId'));

Link.hrefPart is href.split('#')[0], so it never contains '#' and the predicate is never true. The fragment branch of computeBoundaryState is dead code: chapter-button enablement always falls through to findTocIndexByPath(locator, toc, lastMatch: true).

Consequence: in a spine file holding several TOC entries the buttons believe the reader is at the LAST entry in that file, while the tip counter (reader_tip_progress.dart) resolves the FIRST. The two disagree about which chapter the reader is in, which is why the counter's docstring no longer claims parity.

Likely fix: compare link.elementId == tocId, the predicate reader_tip_progress._named uses. That changes button enablement for every book with sub-chapters, so it needs its own tests — reader_navigation_controller_test.dart already has _chapterLocator fixtures to build on.

Found by code review of demo-kuk.

Planning found a second defect in the same function beyond the one reported below: computeBoundaryState passes lastMatch: true for BOTH directions, while TocSkipNavigationMixin._skip passes lastMatch: forward. So on a file holding several entries the previous button is enabled and does nothing when tapped. The fix - delegating to resolveCurrentTocIndex once per direction - covers both, and the slice file carries a boundary case for each.

Cause proven by inspection during code review of demo-kuk: Link.hrefPart strips the fragment, so the predicate at readium_navigation_controller.dart:33 can never be true. Not a blocker for the tip counter, which no longer depends on the buttons agreeing.

title: Debug-only semantics assertion from upstream Flutter 3.44 regression
description:
Debug run threw a framework semantics assertion right after a book finished auto-categorization.

EVIDENCE
Log: /Users/demo/projects/demo/test_logs/debug_output/20260730_224508.log (lines 276-302)
- 22:48:29.734 'Categorization completed for "Majoor Frans" - fiction(google_books)'
- next frame: EXCEPTION CAUGHT BY SCHEDULER LIBRARY
  'package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart' line 6670: failed assertion identical(childRenderObject, parentRenderObject)
  #2 _SemanticsGeometry.computeChildGeometry
  #3 _RenderObjectSemantics._updateChildGeometry
  #5 PipelineOwner.flushSemantics
  #7 RendererBinding.drawFrame
Only reachable with semantics enabled (an accessibility client attached), which is why the normal debug runs stay silent.

LEAD (hypothesis, not yet proven)
features/home/widgets/library_genre_chips.dart hands every genre a GlobalKey (_chipKeys.putIfAbsent) and re-sorts _sortedGenres when the genre set changes. A completed categorization adds a genre, so a keyed chip can move to a new parent inside the same frame - the shape the assertion checks for. Needs confirmation before any fix.

NEXT STEPS
1. Reproduce with semantics on (accessibility client or CarPlay session attached): import a book, let auto-categorization assign its first genre, watch the frame after.
2. Confirm or rule out the genre-chip GlobalKey reparenting with a widget test that swaps the genre list under SemanticsBinding.
3. Check the Flutter tracker for the same assertion signature before changing app code.

Found while verifying demo-84m.2 (CarPlay refresh observer) on the simulator. Unrelated to that change - the Swift observer only repaints CarPlay templates.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — upstream Flutter regression, not app code.

Upstream: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189902 (open, P2, team-accessibility). SemanticsNode._replaceChildren can leave a parent holding a stale child reference; the next flushSemantics then walks a parent/child pair whose render objects are no longer ancestor/descendant and trips the assert. A comment on 2026-07-27 reports this exact assertion (object.dart:6670, _SemanticsGeometry.computeChildGeometry) on Flutter 3.44.8 around overlay dismissal / app focus loss. Reporters saw it start after upgrading 3.38.5 -> 3.44.x. demo runs 3.44.7.

Ruled out in demo (tested, semantics enabled via tester.ensureSemantics()):
- library_genre_chips GlobalKey chips reparenting on the pin/centered layout switch, including add-a-genre while the row still overflows, frame by frame: clean.
- the onboarding firstGenreChipKey moving to a different chip when a genre sorts first: clean.
- keyed first book shifting grid slot when a download placeholder is removed: clean.
- the edit-mode Card -> KeyedSubtree swap that moves firstBookCardKey/firstBookCoverKey: clean.
Also: the log shows Gevoel en verstand already produced fiction+romance at 22:48:14, so the distinct genre set very likely did not change when Majoor Frans completed as fiction at 22:48:29 - the chip-reset path was probably never entered.

Impact: debug only (asserts stripped in profile/release). An attached accessibility client can read stale node geometry while the tree is inconsistent.

Action: blocked on upstream. Documented in demo/docs/04-development/constraints.md -> 'Semantics Assertion in Debug Builds (upstream)'. Re-check on each Flutter stable upgrade; if it becomes disruptive, the fallback is pinning the SDK back to 3.38.5 (user decision, affects the whole toolchain).

Log evidence: /Users/demo/projects/demo/test_logs/debug_output/20260730_224508.log lines 276-302.
